title: Japanese Photography Magazines, 1880s to 1980s
editor: Kaneko Ryuichi; Toda Masako; Ivan Vartanian

description.main: A 500-page history of Japanese photography told through its magazines, from the camera periodicals of the 1880s to the end of the magazine boom in the 1980s, edited by Kaneko Ryūichi, Toda Masako and Ivan Vartanian and published by Goliga with over 1,500 reproductions.
description.extended:
Japanese Photography Magazines, 1880s to 1980s is a 500-page history of Japanese photography told through the magazines that first printed it. It was the last major project of the historian Kaneko Ryūichi.

Kaneko edited it with the photo historian Toda Masako and the publisher Ivan Vartanian. The book runs in three parts, eight chapters and twenty-four sections, from the camera periodicals and amateur clubs of the Meiji era to the close of the magazine boom in the 1980s. Over 1,500 reproductions show feature stories as they ran in Shashin Shinbun, Asahi Graph, Camera Mainichi, Provoke and Shashin Jidai, most of them complete. Fukase Masahisa's Ravens is among them. Each story carries a short commentary, and writings by Araki, Hosoe, Kimura, Moriyama, Terayama and Tanikawa appear in English translation, many for the first time. Captions are bilingual.

The project grew out of Kaneko and Vartanian's Japanese Photobooks of the 1960s and '70s (Aperture, 2009). Vartanian found that the photobook could not be understood apart from the magazines that preceded it. Kaneko, a founding curator of the Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography, died in 2021 before the book appeared. The library also holds his survey with Manfred Heiting, The Japanese Photobook, 1912-1990 (Steidl, 2017).

notes: Shelf: Japanese. Text in English, approx. 200,000 words, with bilingual English and Japanese captions. A Japanese-language edition was published by Heibonsha in 2024 (ISBN 9784582231335).
